glossary.definition: How a portfolio is divided between stocks, bonds, cash and other asset classes.
A decline of 20% or more from a recent high in a broad market index.
A sustained period of rising prices, often measured from a low of 20% or more.
Compound annual growth rate: the smoothed yearly return over a multi-year period.
Investing a fixed amount at regular intervals regardless of price.
The percentage fall from a portfolio’s peak to its subsequent low.
The annual fee a fund charges, as a percentage of assets.
Share price multiplied by shares outstanding: the market value of a company.
Return above the risk-free rate per unit of volatility: higher is better.
Income from an investment (interest or dividends) as a percentage of its price.
